Read a variable without depth from a SpatProxy

Source: R/proxy.R
rast-SpatProxy.Rd

rast() reads time steps of a SpatProxy into memory as plain one-layer terra::SpatRasters. Use it for a variable without depth, such as sea-surface temperature or chlorophyll: each step is one layer named after the variable. A variable with depth stops with an error: read it with as_voxel(), which keeps its depth levels and their edges. So each kind of variable has one reader.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatProxy'
rast(
  x,
  time = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A SpatProxy.

time, time_match, max_time_diff

Which time steps to read, as in as_voxel(): a step number, a date or date-time (matched with time_match, by default to the nearest step), a window of two dates or date-times, or a SpatVector3D with one feature.

...

Not used.

Value

A one-layer terra::SpatRaster, or a list of them, one per step, for a time window or a shape.

Details

The proxy is read as as_voxel() reads it. The time axis is decoded with CFtime rather than by terra, which misreads the time of some files, and the date of each step is set in terra::time(). A proxy cut down with crop() reads only its cells.

mask() by SpatVector3D polygons or points works on the result. It uses only their outlines or positions, not their depths. summarise_3d() also takes the one-layer raster and weights each cell by its area.

Experimental

SpatProxy and as_proxy() are experimental. Their slots and behaviour may change without notice while the core object is built.

See also

as_voxel() for a variable with depth.

Examples

# A 2D temperature field on 1, 3 and 6 January 2020.
p <- as_proxy(system.file("extdata", "example_2d.nc", package = "ocean3d"))
r <- terra::rast(p, time = "2020-01-03")
r
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 2, 2, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1, 1  (x, y)
#> extent      : -0.5, 1.5, 39.5, 41.5  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : temp
#> name        : temp
#> min value   : 15.5
#> max value   : 18.5
#> unit        : degrees_C
#> time        : 2020-01-03 00:00:00zUTC
terra::time(r)
#> [1] "2020-01-03 UTC"

# A window gives one raster per step inside it.
length(terra::rast(p, time = c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-03")))
#> [1] 2

# Summarised with each cell weighted by its area.
summarise_3d(r, statistic = c("mean", "sd"))
#>         time     mean       sd n
#> 1 2020-01-03 16.99266 1.290978 4
